script: If your dog can't stand being more than a few feet away from you, even into the bathroom, there's a real reason behind it. Dogs are famously called velcro dogs when they do this, and it usually comes down to a mix of instinct and learned behavior. Dogs are pack animals, and in the wild, staying close to the group meant safety, food, and protection. You are, functionally, their pack. There's also a strong element of positive reinforcement at play. Every time your dog follows you and something good happens, a treat, attention, a walk, that behavior gets reinforced, so they keep doing it. Breed plays a role too, some breeds were literally developed to work closely alongside humans and are genetically wired to stick close. In most cases, this shadowing behavior is completely normal and even a sign of a secure, trusting bond. But if it becomes extreme, like panic when you're out of sight even for a minute, that can cross into separation anxiety territory. The difference is whether your dog can settle and relax on their own, or whether they're constantly on edge until you're back in view.
